faq.a: Aidar is associated with the Turkic form أَيْدَار, whose core sense is aidar; moon-like (turkic).

faq.q: What is the origin of Aidar?
faq.a: Aidar is associated with Turkic. Aidar is a Turkic (Kazakh/Tatar) male given name, from ay ('moon') + -dar, meaning 'moon-like'.
No — the underlying form is Turkic, not Arabic.
Aidar can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Turkic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Aidar should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Aydar is a Turkic word, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Aidar mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Aidar is rendered ایدار and carries the sense ایدار، چاند جیسا.

faq.q: What does Aidar mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Aidar is rendered آیدار and carries the sense آیدار، ماه‌سان.
A romanized syllable approximation is ai-dar. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Aidar?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Aidar, aidar. Script forms are آیدار, أَيْدَار, ايدار, ایدار, ऐदार.

faq.q: Is Aidar a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
